name: אַהֲרֹן
summary: Aaron the Levite, elder brother of Moses, son of Amram and Jochebed, who spoke for Moses before Pharaoh and was made priest with his sons, the first high priest of Israel, serving at the tent of meeting; he died on Mount Hor. Scripture gives no meaning for his name and no Hebrew word shares its form. Its letters א־ה־ר־ן do not contain the ל of אהל, so it is kept with this root only because the corpus files it here: the evidence does not show a root for it.

evidence.note: “Is not Aaron your brother, the Levite? I know that he can speak well.”
Amram took Jochebed, and she bore him Aaron and Moses.
Aaron was eighty-three years old, three years older than Moses, when they spoke to Pharaoh.
Aaron and his sons brought near to serve Yahweh as priests.
Aaron and his sons coming into the tent of meeting.
In the tent of the testimony, Aaron’s rod for the house of Levi budded.
Aaron died on the top of Mount Hor, and all Israel wept for him thirty days.
No one takes the honour of high priest for himself, but is called by God, as Aaron was.

note: The corpus keys the name under אהל (BDB a.bn.ab, beside אֲהָלִים “aloes”), but the name has ר and ן and no ל, and no Hebrew word or cognate of אהל explains it; the root field follows the corpus key only because a name entry needs one. Suggestions that it is Egyptian were not followed up in the Egyptian dictionary; one proposed source begins with ꜥ, which would appear in Hebrew as ע, not א. Whether to keep Aaron linked to ohel, or give it a root of its own (אהרן) with no entry, is for the reviewer.
